about.what: The audit trail of words.json and the sounds measured inside words. lipsync.py reads "marks" and "breaths"; "changes" is the record.
about.why: The owner asked whether Polly really looks like she is singing; the audit of 13 November 2026 found the speech model's word times wrong at line starts (up to 1.3 s early), words butted end to start so pauses vanished, and consonants laid by arithmetic.
about.how: Read from song.mp3 without any separation model: the centre of the stereo picture (bins where left and right agree), its pitched energy 250-3800 Hz and 150-700 Hz, its 1-3.8 kHz level (falls when the lips or a nasal close the mouth) and its 4.5-9.5 kHz hiss (s, sh, ch, j), in 10 ms steps, with the spectrogram beside them. Precision about 0.03 s in the verses, about 0.06 s where the band is loud (100-117 s).
about.changes: old and new are [start, end] in song seconds; "why" is the evidence. Ends are now where the voice ends, not where the next word starts.
about.marks: start (and end) of one sound of one word, counted from 0 in the word's spelling in lipsync.py; an M, B or P with start and end is the time the lips are shut. Two of the 35 lip closures show no clear dip in the recording and sit at the syllable boundary instead: the M of "moon" (21.5, where the pitch steps up) and the M of "scream" (28.3). "gain" sets how open a sound is drawn at its start and end where the level cannot tell (the band comes back in under the last syllable at 124.27).
about.breaths: audible inhales (unpitched noise in the centre) in pauses; lipsync.py parts the lips for one only where the pause is long enough to stay mostly at rest.
